intent: A tradition traced to its real start: the small host lifts into its flag, the stadium tower is pinned, the Greek flag-ball thinks while the 1896 card says no flame, and then a runner draws the 1936 route from Olympia across seven countries to Berlin with a flash at the lighting in Olympia and a tag for the 3,187 kilometres.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: In which city did the Olympic flame FIRST burn?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: In which city did the Olympic flame first burn?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Amsterdam. In 1928 a flame burned on the stadium's Marathon Tower, lit by a city electricity worker.

lines.direction: ease back over the Low Countries; the Greek flag-ball thinks on 'Athens' with the 1896 card; a candle-out sticker on 'flame'; a tower sticker on 'tower' as the Netherlands pulses; the card leaves at the end
lines.text: Athens revived the Games in 1896 with no flame at all. The Dutch tower simply showed where the Games were.

lines.direction: pull out so Greece and Germany share the frame; the Olympia pin on 'relay'; a white flash on 'Olympia' as a runner sticker rides the drawn line from Olympia to Berlin until 'runners', then the Berlin pin and the kilometres tag; the Netherlands pulses
lines.text: The relay came in 1936: lit in Olympia, carried 3,187 kilometres to Berlin by 3,331 runners.

lines.direction: hold on central Europe with the route lit; a calendar sticker and the days tag on 'twelve'; a clapperboard sticker on 'propaganda' as the German flag-ball thinks; a torch sticker on 'copies' as the Netherlands pulses; the pins leave at the end
lines.text: Twelve days, seven countries, filmed for Nazi propaganda. Every relay since copies that idea.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Lit in Amsterdam first. Follow us.
